g.text: One core module · package-sized boundaries · drivers as plugins · tooling as a separate product
(the missing codemod), not by hand edits
— ONE module, packages as the real boundaries (ADR-0152 end state)
— record · id · dedup · kv · dispatcher · metadata
files: one version train for the domain core
becomes 5 packages with an enforced dependency rule
SPI, registry, capability audit, health/probe, doctor rules
— cost model, planner, layout, hysteresis, calibration, replan
— execute, dispatch, transactions, SSE replay, catch-up
— store, folds, ADTs (vector/graph/spatial/as-of), cursors, typed readers
depends on all, nothing depends on it
ceiling: no package above ~300 exported symbols (today: 829 in one)
Engine drivers stay exactly as they are — the best part of the design
CGo (duckdb) and heavy clients (pg, mysql, pebble, badger) never enter a consumer's graph
Tooling leaves the library's maintenance unit
exporters (22.2k LOC) → own repo(s) or a
-class gates; docs tooling stops competing with the SDK for review time
101 modules → 1 core module + 11 drivers + products: one tag wave instead of 92-tag coordination
829 symbols in one package → ≤300 per package: a change has one obvious home
no v4/v5 mirror twins: one copy of every type, one place to fix a bug
stable vs experimental is a package/repo boundary, not a doc stamp
